passage:
Friday night. Three days since Vinita's catering got the office canteen contract, and I've barely thought about anything else. I told two other stall owners her food is bland. I sent a long message to the market group about "people who undercut everyone." Today I felt good about it for about an hour. Then I saw a missed call from Mrs. Kulkarni, who orders for her daughter's engagement. She'd called twice. I never called back because I was busy checking Vinita's page for reviews. I feel a bit sick. The contract is gone, and now maybe the engagement order too. Tomorrow: call Mrs. Kulkarni first thing. I still don't like Vinita, but she's not the one losing my customers.

Rafiq

qa.q: Which contract did Vinita's catering win?
qa.a: Vinita's catering won the office canteen contract.

qa.q: What is Rafiq feeling toward Vinita, and what does the entry show it has cost him?
qa.a: Rafiq feels bitter and preoccupied, and the obsession cost a missed customer call because Rafiq was busy checking Vinita's reviews.

qa.q: What should Rafiq put his energy into instead of watching Vinita?
qa.a: Call Mrs. Kulkarni back first and give Rafiq's own customers full attention, and maybe learn honestly why the canteen chose Vinita.

qa.q: How might Mrs. Kulkarni have felt when her two calls went unanswered?
qa.a: She may have felt ignored and worried about the engagement order, and might start looking for another caterer.

grounding: Shows a business owner consumed by hatred of a rival who spreads negativity and neglects the business's own customers.

passage:
Shalini: did you see Rahi Tech won the hospital contract?
Baljeet: of course. they're frauds. I've already told three people their software crashes
Shalini: does it?
Baljeet: probably
Shalini: Baljeet. you've spent the whole week on them. checking their posts, their hires, their prices
Baljeet: someone has to
Shalini: meanwhile our own client from Pune emailed twice about the login bug and nobody answered
Baljeet: they'll wait
Shalini: they won't. they just told me they're thinking of leaving
Baljeet: ...what?
Shalini: I'm worried about you. and about us. we're losing our own customers while you watch theirs
Baljeet: I just hate that they're winning
Shalini: I know. but hating them isn't a plan. fixing our login bug is
Baljeet: ok. I'll call Pune now

qa.q: How many people had Baljeet told that the rival's software crashes?
What was Baljeet feeling about Rahi Tech?
qa.a: Baljeet felt bitter hatred and envy, saying they hated that the rival was winning.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could fix it?
qa.a: Obsession with the rival made Baljeet spread negativity and ignore their own client's login bug; refocusing on customers and fixing the bug could fix it.

qa.q: How does Shalini see Baljeet's behaviour?
qa.a: Shalini is worried about Baljeet and the business, seeing the obsession with the rival as costing them their own customers.

grounding: Shows how hatred of a rival leads a young worker to spread negativity and neglect customers, and how refocusing helps.

passage:
When Madhav opened a new sweet shop across the square in Karad, he took most of the Diwali box orders in his first year.

Hrithik, whose family shop had stood there for forty years, couldn't stop watching. He counted Madhav's customers from behind his own counter. He told anyone who would listen that Madhav used cheap ghee. None of it was true, and he knew it.

Meanwhile the jalebis in his own shop went soggy because nobody minded the oil. A regular customer, Shobha-tai, returned a box of stale pedhas. Hrithik barely noticed.

His father noticed. One evening he sat Hrithik down. "Your grandfather never once talked about another shop. He talked about his sweets." He placed the returned box on the counter. "You're losing our customers yourself."

Hrithik stared at the box for a long time. The next morning he stood at the frying pan himself, and he stopped saying anything at all about Madhav.

qa.a: Shobha-tai returned a box of stale pedhas.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling as he counted Madhav's customers?
qa.a: Hrithik felt jealous and resentful, obsessed with the rival's success.

qa.q: What went wrong for Hrithik, and what did he do to fix it?
qa.a: Spreading false rumours and watching the rival made him neglect his own sweets and lose customers; he returned to the frying pan and stopped talking about Madhav.

qa.q: How does Hrithik's father see what is happening?
qa.a: His father sees that the obsession with Madhav, not Madhav himself, is costing the family shop its customers.

grounding: Shows how a young shop owner's hatred of a rival leads him to spread negativity and lose customers, and how he turns back to his own work.
